reason: The text explicitly portrays the Israelites as devoted followers of Yahweh. Moses and the children of Israel sing directly to the LORD (לַֽיהוָה), declaring 'I will sing to the LORD' (אָשִׁ֤ירָה לַֽיהוָה), calling him 'my God' (אֵלִי), identifying him as 'the God of my father,' and celebrating his power and victories. Throughout the passage, Yahweh (יְהוָה) is invoked repeatedly as their deliverer, protector, and the supreme God ('Who is like you among the gods, O LORD?'). Their worship, praise, and reliance on his guidance and strength clearly establish them as followers of the God Yahweh.
